title.en: Revenue, expenses, profit, gain and loss

body.en: Revenue is the amount earned from the regular business activity, such as sales, commission or interest received. Expenses are costs incurred to earn revenue, such as rent, wages and salaries. Expenditure is spending of money: revenue expenditure benefits one year, capital expenditure benefits many years. Profit is the excess of revenue over expenses; a gain is profit from an event of a non-recurring nature, such as selling an old machine above book value; a loss is the opposite.
body.kn: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ವ್ಯವಹಾರದಿಂದ ಬರುವ ಹಣ ಆದಾಯ. ಆದಾಯ ಗಳಿಸಲು ಮಾಡುವ ಖರ್ಚು ವೆಚ್ಚ. ಆದಾಯ ವೆಚ್ಚಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದ್ದರೆ ಲಾಭ. ಅಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಘಟನೆಯಿಂದ ಬರುವ ಲಾಭ ಗಳಿಕೆ.

title.en: On the board: Revenue, profit and discounts

say.en: Kiran Traders sold goods costing 40 thousand for 52 thousand. First, gross profit.
Rent and wages are expenses. Deduct them to get net profit.
Now discounts. List price 20 thousand, 10 percent trade discount, 2 percent cash discount.
Trade discount is never recorded. Only the cash discount of 360 is entered as discount allowed.

prompt.en: Sort each term into its class.

explanation.en: Revenues are earned from business activity; expenses are costs of earning them; assets are resources the business owns; liabilities are amounts it owes to outsiders.

title.en: Goods, stock, debtors, creditors, discount and voucher

body.en: Goods are the items a business buys to sell. Purchases are goods bought for resale, for cash or on credit; sales are goods sold. Stock (inventory) is goods lying unsold on a date. Debtors owe money to the business; creditors are owed money by the business. Trade discount is a reduction in list price and is not recorded in the books; cash discount is allowed for prompt payment and is recorded. A voucher is the written evidence for an entry.
body.kn: ಮಾರಾಟಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಕೊಳ್ಳುವ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಸರಕು. ಮಾರಾಟವಾಗದೆ ಉಳಿದವು ದಾಸ್ತಾನು. ಋಣಿಗಳು ನಮಗೆ ಕೊಡಬೇಕು; ಧನಿಗಳಿಗೆ ನಾವು ಕೊಡಬೇಕು. ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ರಿಯಾಯಿತಿ ದಾಖಲಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ನಗದು ರಿಯಾಯಿತಿ ದಾಖಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Kiran Traders sold goods costing ₹40,000 for ₹52,000. It paid rent ₹3,000 and wages ₹2,000 for the period. Find the gross profit and the net profit.

steps.en: Gross profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold = ₹52,000 − ₹40,000 = ₹12,000.
